decision_conditions: <p>A scheme for the provision and implementation of flood resilient and resistant construction details and measures for the lower ground floor and outbuilding against surface water flood risk shall be submitted to and agreed, in writing with the LPA in consultation with the LLFA prior to the construction of the measures. The scheme shall be carried out in its entirety before the sites are occupied and; constructed and completed in accordance with the approved plans in line with current best practices.</p><p><br></p><p>REASON: In the interest of mitigating flood risk.</p>

<p>Prior to the commencement of the relevant part of the work, the applicant shall submit, and have approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, a detailed layout, cross sections (scale 1:20), full specifications and a detailed management and maintenance plan of the biodiverse roof with a minimum substrate depth of 80mm, not including the vegetative mat. The development shall not be carried out otherwise than in accordance with the details thus approved and shall be fully implemented before the premises are first occupied.</p><p><br></p><p>REASON: In the interests of biodiversity and sustainable drainage.&nbsp;</p>

The Development hereby permitted shall only be carried out and completed strictly in accordance with the submitted plans hereby approved and any subsequent approval of details.


REASON: To ensure that the development hereby permitted is carried out in full accordance with the plans hereby approved.

The development hereby permitted must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of this permission.


REASON: In order to comply with the provisions of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended).

subdivision_of_building: The application relates to several small amendments to the rear extension on the south facing facade only - at ground (G) and lower ground (LG),
description:
The renovation of 222 Richmond Road is currently underway in accordance with approved planning consent (2023/0256). 

Since consent was granted in 2023 the home owner has been diagnosed with Parkinsons’ disease and now requires disabled access between the lower ground, garden and ground level. We therefore wish to apply for ammendments to the approved planning consent that concern wheel chair access at the rear elevation of the property. 

KEY DESIGN PRINCIPLES

The aim of this application is to demonstrate that the proposed works will not have a detrimental impact on the existing historic character whilst improving the disabled access to the property for the homeowner.

WHEELCHAIR PLATFORM LIFT

We would like to install an external platform lift at the rear of the property to facilitate wheel chair access. Having consulted with a lift engineer we propose locating the lift in a discrete position at the rear of the property, where it can service the lower ground, garden and ground floor levels.

AMMENDED DESIGN OF GARDEN DOOR

The current approved planning allows for a garden door on the rear facade at ground level. The door is flanked on each side by fixed windows. We’d like to keep the scale and fenestartion of the door exactly the same as the approved permision, but lose the fixed windows on each side of the door. Wheel chair access will be improved by creating a straight pathway between the rear door and the garden.

PRE-APPLICATON ADVICE (2025/0067/PA) 

The proposals here were shared with our Hackney planning officer, Zarreen Hadadi and the design team, for a pre-application consultation (2025/0067/PA). This application has been adjusted in response to the advice provided.
